comment: The bucket's CORS policy (docs/national-scaleout.md §3), committed because it
is coupled to something that moves: the app's own origin.
Every bundle the app reads is cross-origin — the app is served from
fornborgar.drnz.se and the bytes come from the object host — so a browser
only ever sees data from a host whose allowlist names the app's origin. When
it does not, fetch() rejects at the network layer and the app reports
'Failed to fetch' with no status to go on. That is what a domain move breaks,
and it breaks it silently, which is why the policy lives here rather than only
(no flag shows the live policy and the diff against this file).
The github.io origin is the pre-move Pages one, kept so a rollback to the
project-site URL still loads; the localhost/127.0.0.1 pairs are `npm run dev`
and `npm run preview` with VITE_DATA_BASE_URL set against the live bucket.
`exposeHeaders` is not decoration: geotiff.js reads the grids with range
requests, and without content-range/accept-ranges exposed they fail to decode
